To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the UHECR spectrum can be understood in the framework of a single source model, and the source model is consistent with the observed UHECR spectrum, with the observed anisotropy of the UHECR flux and with the observed UHCR photon flux.

(i) the UHECR spectrum can be described by a power law with an energy dependent spectral index, (ii) the spectral index is not a function of the primary mass, and (iii) there are no significant deviations from the power law spectrum at any energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the fundamental structure of matter.
the study of high energy particle physics, in particular, the study of the properties of particles with high energy and the study of the interactions of particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UHECR problem remains open and that no single solution has emerged from the plethora of ideas proposed so far.
there are no convincing arguments for any of the models discussed in this paper to explain the observed data of ultra-high energy cosmic rays.
the UHECRs have been observed to be of extragalactic origin and that they are likely to be protons, with the exception of a small fraction of the events at the highest energies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the UHECRs are not the most energetic particles in the Universe, and the most energetic particles are not the UHECR.
we have demonstrated that the cosmic ray data is consistent with a top down model of cosmic rays and neutrinos, and that it is not consistent with the bottom up models.

the Z-burst model, the topological defect model, the strongly interacting neutrino model, the violation of LorentZ invariance model, and the super-massive dark matter models are all viable solutions to the UHCR puzzle, and that the new primary model and the neutrino decay model are not viable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the universe is not as we thought.
there are no new particles in the Standard Model that can produce UHE cosmic rays.
we can now say that the UHECRs are likely to be protons and nuclei, and not photons, with energies of order 10 20 eV.
